oewn-00590283-v.learner: to know what someone or something is really like, or what it means.
examples: the experience of three-and-twenty years had been insufficient to make his wife understand his character

oewn-00594917-v.learner: to believe that something is true.
examples: I understood that there were some very strong objections against the lady.

oewn-00592510-v.learner: to take in an idea or a situation in your mind.
examples: Elizabeth soon observed, and instantly understood it.

oewn-15259561-n.learner: a length of time of sixty seconds, which is one sixtieth of an hour.
examples: Mr. Bingley returned Mr. Bennet's visit, and sat about ten minutes with him in his library.
She then sat still five minutes longer

oewn-15271664-n.learner: a short piece of time of no fixed length.
examples: I will be with you in a minute.
The minute she saw him, she knew something was wrong.

oewn-02643676-v.learner: to be what is left over, whether of people, questions, problems, results, or evidence.
examples: And now nothing remains for me but to assure you in the most animated language of the violence of my affection.
the conjectures of the remaining three continued, though with little satisfaction

oewn-00117793-v.learner: to stay the same, going on in one state.
examples: Of the lady's sensations they remained a little in doubt
Mr. Darcy walked off; and Elizabeth remained with no very cordial feelings towards him.

oewn-02733337-v.learner: to go on being in a place, a position, or a situation.
examples: Mrs. Bennet, who had calculated on her daughters remaining at Netherfield till the following Tuesday

oewn-01861378-v.learner: to be in a place and not go away from it.
examples: he found Lydia absolutely resolved on remaining where she was.
Mr. Darcy had at first scarcely allowed her to be pretty
whether she wished or feared it most, she could scarcely determine

oewn-00002669-r.learner: only a very short time earlier.
examples: He had scarcely sat down when the bell rang.

oewn-01235721-n.learner: the act of going to see a person, a place, or a thing for a short time.
examples: She wrote again when the visit was paid, and she had seen Miss Bingley.

oewn-01057284-n.learner: a stay somewhere for a while, for example as someone's guest.
examples: In this quiet way the first fortnight of her visit soon passed away.

oewn-01235249-n.learner: the act of going to see someone in their line of work.
examples: She paid a visit to the lawyer to ask about her father's will.

oewn-07560785-n.learner: a warm, friendly feeling of respect for someone.
examples: I have an excessive regard for Jane Bennet,--she is really a very sweet girl

oewn-05828314-n.learner: one detail or point of a matter.
examples: he had either been deceived with regard to her fortune
mentioned with raptures some plans of the latter with regard to new furniture

oewn-14461018-n.learner: the state of being honoured and thought well of by others.
examples: She is held in high regard by everyone who works with her.
Elizabeth listened with delight to the happy though modest hopes which Jane entertained of Bingley's regard
Elizabeth listened as little as she could, but there was no escaping the frequent mention of Wickham's name.

oewn-02175483-v.learner: to listen to someone and take notice of what they say.
examples: She would not listen, therefore, to her daughter's proposal of being carried home

oewn-02577816-v.learner: to give close attention to someone or something.
examples: She listened most attentively to all that passed between them
What do you think has happened this morning?
how many things have happened!

oewn-02600068-v.learner: to be or do something by chance, with no one meaning it or making it so.
examples: Jane happened to look round
her husband's regiment happens to be so far off.

oewn-00345297-v.learner: to take place, or turn out to be so, as events go along or by chance.
examples: Whatever happens to her, she will face it bravely.

oewn-08662297-n.learner: land that lies outside cities and towns.
examples: His coming into the country at all is a most insolent thing, indeed

oewn-08185877-n.learner: a body of people organised under one government.
examples: The country elected a new government last year.

oewn-08562388-n.learner: the land that a nation holds.
examples: The river runs the whole length of the country.

oewn-00075427-r.learner: in, to, or toward a place where someone or something was before.
examples: I shall be back by dinner.
I am glad you are come back, Lizzy.

oewn-00074673-r.learner: at, to, or toward the back or the rear.
examples: Miss Austen, too, drew back when the white frost touched her shoes

oewn-00075535-r.learner: in, to, or toward the condition something was in at the start.
examples: After the fever passed, he went back to his old self.
